audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows contradicted the why sitting on them. whys[0] opens 'Jayce owns level 1' on a Mordekaiser row rated 7/10. whys[2] opens 'Level 3 is yours' on a Jayce row. whys[3] says 'Skill window' on a Jayce row. whys[5] says your first item makes the all-in lethal on a Jayce row. whys[6] says 'the duel stays a coinflip' on a Jayce row.
audit.why: The packet chart — Jayce / Skill / Mordekaiser / Skill / Mordekaiser / Mordekaiser / Skill — matches every one of the seven whys exactly. The content prose on this page is well written and was simply not reflected in the chart on either layer.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 5 and 6 flipped as one atomic group in both layers to Jayce 3/10, Mordekaiser 7/10, Skill 5/10, Mordekaiser 7/10, Skill 5/10, with phases[3].why and phases[6].why rewritten to argue their new side.

audit.why: Spikes are right and honest about the shape of the lane: Jayce owns 1-2, level 3 is where your E arrives, level 6 is the Realm, first item is the lethal all-in. Nothing to move.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere for a matchup whose entire plan is 'walk up when his poke is down'. breakdown.cooldowns listed Q twice with no numbers. Nothing states that his first attack after swapping to cannon shreds your resistances.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16/14/12/10/8/6 — 16 seconds at rank 1, which is a genuinely large walk-up window, and 6 seconds maxed, which is why the same advice stops working later. Thundering Blow is 20/18/16/14/12/10 and is the knockback that cancels your engage, so it is the ability to bait before spending Death's Grasp. Riot's R text says the first attack in cannon form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist, so the stance swap is a visible tell for incoming shred.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns for Q, E and the stance swap written into breakdown.cooldowns; 16s into dosFull[0].d; 20s into dontsFull[1].d; the resist shred into dontsFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file says your Obliterate shuts off Jayce's To the Skies! and tells you to hold Q for the engage. Riot's Obliterate text does not support any grounding effect.
audit.why: The kit file's derived 'grounding' flag on Mordekaiser's Q misfires — Riot's description is only a ground smash dealing damage, increased against a single target. Writing 'hold Q to deny his leap' would be a fabricated mechanic on the single most-read line of the page.
audit.corrected: Not written. The walk-up advice is keyed to Shock Blast's 16s cooldown and to the 700-unit Death's Grasp range instead, both of which are verifiable.

edits.before: Q ranks make isolated hits massive. Jayce must hug minions all lane; punish every step away from the wave with the full drag combo.
edits.after: Q ranks hit hard, but he swaps to cannon and pokes from outside your 700-unit Death's Grasp — knife-edge unless you land E.

edits.before: Riftmaker omnivamp turns the Realm 1v1 unloseable into most matchups. Jayce's only outs are dodging Q forever or never being alone — neither survives a whole game.
edits.after: Riftmaker keeps the Realm 1v1 yours, but a fed Jayce chunks you before you ever land E — a coinflip decided by whether Realm of Death is up when he steps in.

notes: Both flagged suspectNames are false positives: 'Bank Indestructible' is the real name with a verb in front, and 'Shock Blasts' is the real name used as a verb. No name changes made. The important non-edit: missingInteractions claims Obliterate grounds and denies Jayce's To the Skies!, sourced from the kit file's derived 'grounding' flag on Mordekaiser's Q. Riot's own Obliterate description contains nothing of the kind, and per the trust-the-description rule I did not write it — it would have been the most actionable-sounding line on the page and completely made up. The same flag has now misfired on every matchup in this slice, which suggests it is a champion-level tooltip-parsing fault on Mordekaiser's Q rather than anything matchup-specific; worth fixing at the kit level so no future agent writes it in.
